summary: An excerpt from a fiction work ("Book 10 — part 145") in which an envoy named Leon meets a woman called Ria in a richly designed room in Ate. The two share an easy, playful rapport: Ria kicks off her shoes and sits cross-legged on a topiary chair, Leon removes his handmade shoes and socks and sits barefoot on the mossy floor, and they laugh together over whether anyone has ever done something mischievous in the room. The passage ends with Ria saying they should get to the matter at hand.
one_line: Envoy Leon meets Ria, a warm, unpretentious woman, in a striking room in Ate, and they bond over going barefoot and laughter.
key_facts: Leon is an envoy who is out of place in Ate, though Ate's people do not hold it against the envoy.
Leon first meets Ria in the Living Room, which he finds fantastic and impressive.
Ria is estimated to be around 40 years old, is hippy and a little wrinkled, and has iron-grey hair.
Ria wears sensible jeans and comfortable hush puppies.
Ria introduces herself as Ria and asks Leon to call her that.
Ria sits cross-legged on one of the topiary chairs after kicking off her hush puppies.
Ria insists that Leon go barefoot in the room, saying "Do it! I insist. Do it!"
Leon's handmade shoes were designed by an architect who gave up on literary criticism to pursue cobblery.
The ground in the room feels pleasantly tingling on Leon's feet, with a texture he cannot pin down, warm or cool.
Ria says she is wondering whether anyone has ever snuck into the room and screwed on the stuff.
Leon sits on the mossy floor, letting it brush against his feet, ankles, palms and wrists.
Leon and Ria laugh hard together until their stomachs hurt.
Leon says that if no one has ever done it, it is a damned shame.
Ria offers food and drink, noting that almost anything can be obtained in the room, before saying "Let's get to it."
